title: Dynamic regulation of integrin β1 phosphorylation supports invasion of breast cancer cells
projectDescription: Integrins provide an essential bridge between cancer cells and the extracellular matrix, playing a central role in every stage of disease progression. Despite the recognized significance of integrin phosphorylation in several biological processes, the regulatory mechanisms and their relevance remained elusive. To address this gap, we engineered a fluorescence resonance energy transfer biosensor for integrin β1 phosphorylation, screening 96 protein tyrosine phosphatases and identifying Shp2 and PTP-PEST as negative regulators. Mutation of the integrin NPxY(783/795) sites revealed the importance of integrin phosphorylation for efficient cancer cell invasion, further supported by inhibition of the identified integrin phosphorylation regulators Shp2 and Src kinase. Using proteomics approaches, we uncovered Cofilin as a component of the phosphorylated integrin-Dok1 complex and linked this axis to effective invadopodia formation, a process supporting breast cancer invasion. These data further implicate dynamic modulation of integrin β1 phosphorylation at NPxY sites at different stages of metastatic dissemination.
sampleProcessingProtocol: BiCAP proteomics was performed in HEK293T cells transfected with either pDEST-ITGB1-V1/pDEST-Dok1-V2 or control pEF.DEST51-mVenus using Lipofectamine 3000 (ThermoFisher) in OptiMEM (Gibco, 31985070), as per the manufacturer’s protocol. After an overnight incubation, cells were lysed in immunoprecipitation (IP) lysis buffer (40 mM HEPES, 75 mM NaCl, 2 mM EDTA, 1% NP-40, along with protease (cOmpleteTM Mini, EDTA-free, Roche) and phosphatase (PhosSTOP, Roche) inhibitor cocktails), and subjected to IP using GFP-trap beads (30 μl, Chromotek, gfa), at 4oC with gentle agitation for 1 hour. Samples were then spun down at 300 g for 5 minutes and the beads washed thrice with PBS and once with 50 mM Tris–HCl, pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl. For the on-bead digestion, samples were reduced with 10 mM DTT/50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0 in the presence of 8 M urea for 1 hour at 37oC, then alkylated in 40 mM iodoacetamide/50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0 for 1 hour in the dark. DTT was then added in excess to consume the remaining alkylating agent and dilute the urea before overnight digestion with trypsin (Promega, V5111) at 37oC. Samples were then acidified with TFA pH ~2 before desalting using Sep-Pak C18 96-well plates (Waters, 186002321). LC-MS/MS was then performed with 300 ng of sample for the analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: Assignment of peptides and quantification of abundance ratios (normalized to total peptide amount) by label-free quantification was performed in Proteome Discoverer 2.5 (ThermoFisher) using intensity values from the precursor ions.
